gold_rationale: AAV-GDNF to the putamen by CED has a plausible trophic rationale, but prior GDNF/neurturin PD gene-therapy and protein-infusion trials largely failed on efficacy with putaminal coverage/biodistribution repeatedly implicated, and the current constitutive design lacks dose control and reversibility despite dose-dependent GDNF off-target effects (sprouting, host TH downregulation, weight loss, cerebellar toxicity) and anti-GDNF immunogenicity. Progression should be a Conditional Go contingent on demonstrating adequate putaminal coverage (CED with intraoperative imaging), adding a regulatable/reversible dose-control strategy, dose-ranging and biodistribution studies, capsid/transgene immune management, patient stratification, and a sham-controlled biomarker/endpoint plan. A defensible alternative is No-Go for the constitutive, uncontrolled design as presented. Treating 'GDNF is neuroprotective, so it will work' as settled is wrong given prior trial failures.
required_concepts: prior GDNF/neurturin PD trial failures (coverage implicated)
putaminal coverage / biodistribution as the gating problem
lack of dose control / reversibility (constitutive AAV)
red_flags: assumes GDNF will work because it is neuroprotective, ignoring prior trial failures
ignores putaminal coverage / biodistribution as the central design problem
ignores lack of dose control / reversibility of a constitutive AAV-GDNF transgene
ignores GDNF dose-dependent off-target effects or anti-GDNF immunogenicity
claims demonstrated efficacy without a sham-controlled design
